subject.title: [Bug]: exec tool treats subprocess nonzero exit codes as tool failures, masking stdout and exit-code semantics

question: Should ordinary completed exec subprocess exits with nonzero codes become normal agent-visible results by default, or should OpenClaw require an explicit accepted-exit-code option?
rationale: The root cause is narrow, but the permanent fix changes the meaning of nonzero exec exits for existing cron/tool workflows and may affect failure alerts.

options.title: Default normal completed exits
options.body: Treat normal process exits as successful tool transport regardless of exit code, while preserving failures for spawn/runtime errors, timeouts, signals, and shell 126/127.

options.title: Add explicit accepted exit codes
options.body: Keep the current default failure classification and add an opt-in tool option such as acceptedExitCodes or allowNonzeroExit for semantic scripts.

options.title: Document wrapper-only behavior
options.body: Keep current behavior and document the always-exit-zero wrapper pattern for semantic exit-code workflows.

recommendation.title: Default normal completed exits
recommendation.body: Treat normal process exits as successful tool transport regardless of exit code, while preserving failures for spawn/runtime errors, timeouts, signals, and shell 126/127.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the best available routing candidate from current checked-out blame and prior adjacent triage on the exec exit-code behavior.
